description: A ten-panel composite figure (five columns × two rows, mildly mixed modalities) comparing impact-deformed samples at RT (a–e) and LNT (f–j). (a, f) are macroscopic photographs of the fractured Charpy specimens with a 10 cm scale bar, annotated "main crack", "subordinate cracks" and "necking" (green dashed), plus a dashed rectangle marking the EBSD zone. (b, g) are EBSD phase maps (20 µm scale bar) that are almost entirely blue γ with a minute red α fraction; white arrows label "Main crack" and "Impact direction", and the inset sketches the specimen with black dots marking the analysed positions (10 cm). (c, h) are IPF maps along the impact direction (20 µm) with an IPF colour triangle and "-15°<θ" / "59°<θ" annotations. (d, i) are bright-field TEM images taken ~1000 µm from the fracture surface (500 nm scale bars) labelled "twins" (white dashed arrows) and "Microbands?" (green), each with a square-pattern SAED inset. (e, j) are SEM fracture surfaces (20 µm) showing dimples. Taken together the panels argue that impact deformation proceeds by dislocation cells plus twinning with no phase transformation, that both fractures are dimpled/ductile, and that LNT additionally forms fine cracks at γ/α interfaces.

subfigures.description: Macroscopic photograph of the room-temperature impact fracture, with 10 cm scale bar, labelled 'main crack', 'subordinate cracks' (white text) and 'necking' (green dashed outline); a dashed white rectangle marks the EBSD sampling area. Large necking and many subordinate cracks are visible.

EBSD phase map near the RT fracture surface (20 µm scale bar): background almost entirely blue (γ, austenite) with only a tiny red area labelled α; white arrows mark 'Main crack' and 'Impact direction'. Inset: schematic specimen sketch (10 cm scale) with black dots indicating the analysed zone.

Colour IPF map along the impact direction near the RT fracture surface (20 µm scale bar) with an IPF colour triangle legend (top right) and annotations '-15°<θ' and '59°<θ'; large colour-contrasted grains and elongated deformation features.

Bright-field TEM image of the RT sample ~1000 µm from the fracture surface (500 nm scale bar); white dashed arrows point to features labelled 'twins', a green dashed label reads 'Microbands?'. Inset SAED pattern with dotted square indicating spot reflections.
SEM image of the RT fracture surface (20 µm scale bar) showing equiaxed dimples of micrometre/sub-micrometre size, i.e. a ductile fracture morphology.

Macroscopic photograph of the LNT impact fracture, 10 cm scale bar, labelled 'main crack', 'subordinate cracks' and 'necking' (green dashed); necking and the number of subordinate cracks appear smaller than in (a).

EBSD phase map near the LNT fracture surface (20 µm scale bar) dominated by blue γ with a small α fraction; red arrows point to fine cracks around voids; white arrows mark 'Main crack' and 'Impact direction'. Inset: specimen sketch (10 cm) with black dots for the analysed location.

Colour IPF map along the impact direction near the LNT fracture surface (20 µm scale bar) with IPF triangle legend and '-15°<θ' / '59°<θ' annotations; strongly banded/elongated colour contrast suggests twinning and slip bands.

Bright-field TEM image of the LNT sample ~1000 µm from the fracture surface (500 nm scale bar); white dashed arrows label 'twins', green dashed label 'Microbands?'. Inset SAED pattern with dotted square marker.
SEM image of the LNT fracture surface (20 µm scale bar) showing dimples with some larger deep voids; still a ductile dimpled morphology.

observations.observation: Panel (a) (RT, 10 cm scale bar) shows the macroscopic impact fracture with a large number of subordinate cracks and pronounced necking; panel (f) (LNT, same 10 cm scale) shows fewer subordinate cracks and smaller necking.
The EBSD phase maps (b, g, 20 µm scale bars) are nearly all blue phase γ with only a very small red region assigned to α; no resolvable phase transformation product is visible in the mapped areas.
Red arrows in panel (g) point to fine cracks located around voids in the LNT sample.
The IPF maps (c, h, 20 µm scale bars) carry an IPF colour-triangle legend and the misorientation annotations '-15°<θ' and '59°<θ'.

The TEM images (d, i, 500 nm scale bars) contain white dashed arrows labelled 'twins' and a green dashed label 'Microbands?', and each has an SAED inset whose dotted square indicates the indexed reflections.
The fracture surfaces (e, j, 20 µm scale bars) consist of micrometre to sub-micrometre dimples at both test temperatures.

The caption states that (a, f) are macroscopic fracture appearances, (b, g) phase maps near the fracture surface, (c, h) IPF maps along the impact direction, (d, i) TEM maps ~1000 µm from the fracture surface, and (e, j) fracture surface maps; note the caption's parenthetical '(f–g)' appears to be a typographical error for '(f–j)'.
The citing text states that EBSD was performed in the typical crack propagation zone, marked by the black dots in the inset of Fig. 9(b–g).
The citing text states that the samples remain highly stable at both room temperature and liquid nitrogen temperature, with no phase transformation occurring in the austenite.
The citing text states that dislocation substructures at both temperatures consist of dislocation cells or cell blocks, similar to the substructure under tension.
The citing text states that low temperature promotes the formation of deformation twins, as seen in Fig. 9(c, d, h, i).

The citing text attributes the fine cracks around voids in the cryogenic sample to detachment of α, making the γ/α interface the crack initiation site, and reports impact energy falling about 30 % from 331 J at RT to 254 J at LNT due to 3.0 % α-phase in the austenite matrix.
The citing text interprets (e, j) as showing that the fracture surfaces consist mainly of micrometre to sub-micrometre dimples at both RT and LNT, i.e. ductile fracture at both temperatures.

IPF colour-triangle legends in (c)/(h): individual orientation labels on the triangle are not readable
SAED insets in (d)/(i): diffraction spot labels/indices are not printed legibly
the caption's panel range '(f–g)' conflicts with the pixel panels (f–j); the pixel layout was used
